summary: Round 4, prose only: ADR-0044, an ADR-0043 Status/body amendment, revision banners on five research sections, SubscriptionEvent and SubscriptionEventGrantTest javadoc, M5.66, M5.45f done. No production logic, no wire change, no object-store request added, moved or authorised anywhere in this diff, and the request-rate framing in the new prose is the right one throughout (the coalescing target is ONE WHOLE-OBJECT GET per (node, segment), never per run; M5.66's cell prices directory-then-slice as two-against-one and demands NO MORE requests at the ~400-run share). THE FIVE ROUND-3 FINDINGS ARE FIXED: 50-open-questions Q8 now carries a banner at :48-57 and a sweep row; ADR-0043's Status says 'NOT closed ... it now has an OWNER'; (b1)'s corpus argument is explicitly withdrawn at :211-220; the price is derived once at :106-148 and I re-derived every figure independently (7/129 = 5.43%, 11,200/8,388,608 = 0.1335%, 206,400/8,388,608 = 2.4605%, 0.1335/2.4605 = 5.43%, 40.4x -- the cross-check holds); M5.66's criterion 3 now points at the table instead of copying it. I CHECKED THE UNASKED-FOR CORRECTION AGAINST SOURCE AND IT IS RIGHT: SegmentWriter:90 sets headerLen = runCount * DIRECTORY_ENTRY_BYTES (the directory alone, preamble excluded) and SegmentReader:78 CRCs [PREAMBLE, PREAMBLE+headerLen), so [0, PREAMBLE + headerLen) is exactly preamble-plus-directory; SegmentPublisher:147 computes PREAMBLE_BYTES + SegmentKey.headerLenOf(key) - 1 as an inclusive end; SegmentKey.headerLenOf is public and in `format`, which `client` depends on, and SubscriptionEvent carries segmentKey -- so the consumer can name that range; and SegmentFormat:17 does put u32 codecFlags in the directory entry while the DATA framing at :20 is [u32 uncompressedLen][u32 crc32c][records] with no codec id, so a reader holding the directory holds the flags. The correction is better supported than the claim it replaces. WHAT BLOCKS IS THAT THE CORRECTION WAS APPLIED IN FIVE PLACES AND THE SUPERSEDED CLAIM IS STILL ASSERTED IN FOUR MORE, THREE OF THEM WRITTEN BY THIS COMMIT -- including ADR-0044's own Decision (c), its own alternative (b3), and a NEW revision banner on doc 10 section 8, which under AGENTS.md WINS over the prose it corrects. That is the one-of-two-places defect this task has now reproduced in every round, this time inside the fix for it. Separately, the sweep table that M5.66's criterion 3 makes THE enumeration is split in two by a paragraph, stranding seven of its nineteen rows outside both the sentence and the rendered table, and M5.45f's own done-cell calls a modelled number MEASURED in the same cell that corrects that exact error.

findings.title: Decision (c) still answers security.md rule 3 with 'no range is expressible for the reasons under (b)' -- and (b) now says two ranges ARE expressible
findings.summary: :163-166 reads 'the grant is scoped to one key and to no range, and "where possible one range" is not possible today -- no range is expressible for the reasons under (b), so there is nothing for a signature to cover.' Decision (b), 78 lines above in the same file, now says the opposite in a table it added this round: :86 '[0, PREAMBLE + headerLen) -- preamble plus directory | YES | that is exactly what SegmentKey's h<headerLen> is for, and SegmentPublisher.headerRangeEndInclusive computes it in the tree today', :87 'a run's DATA slice [byteStart, byteStart + byteLen) | YES as a request', and :91 'SO A BOUNDED READ IS TWO EXPRESSIBLE REQUESTS, NOT AN IMPOSSIBILITY'. The cross-reference 'for the reasons under (b)' therefore points at the text that refutes it. The conclusion (c) reaches is still right for a different reason -- the only read the consumer path makes today is a whole-object GET, so there is no range for a signature to cover -- which is precisely the 'the conclusion holds, the reason given for it does not' form this commit uses on doc 10 section 8 and on 50-open-questions Q8.
findings.failure_scenario: ADR-0041:114 defers security.md rule 3's range half and the chain reaches this record; ADR-0043's amended Status and body both send an auditor here, and M5.66's criterion 4 names (c) as the statement of the clause's status. The next security pass -- or M5.66's owner discharging criterion 4 -- reads (c), takes 'no range is expressible' as the capability statement, and either declines the clause as physically impossible or records it as unanswerable. Both are false of the tree as this same record documents it: a consumer holding segmentKey can name [0, PREAMBLE + headerLen) today, and a grant could in principle be signed to it. The reader has no way to tell which half of the record to believe, and the half they land on is the one written under the rule's own heading.
findings.suggested_fix: Restate (c) on the reason that survives: the only read the consumer path makes today is a whole-object GET, so the grant is scoped to one key and to no range and there is nothing for a signature to cover; a range becomes signable when M5.66 lands the entry point that makes the two-request read usable. Delete 'no range is expressible for the reasons under (b)'.

findings.title: Alternative (b3) still prices the bounded reader at 'two things the current layout forbids', including the codec objection the same record says dissolves -- the phrase the backlog cell corrected and the ADR did not
findings.summary: :227-233 rejects landing the bounded reader now because 'It needs a SegmentReader that can decode from a slice, which means solving two things the current layout forbids: the footer magic is checked before the directory, and u32 codecFlags lives per run in the directory while DATA carries no codec id -- so a ranged GET of a run's DATA slice cannot decompress what it fetched.' :91-99 of the same file retires exactly that: 'the codec objection dissolves with it: a reader that fetched the header HAS the directory, so it has the per-run codecFlags ... What is actually absent is narrower than earlier drafts of this record said: a SegmentReader entry point that takes a directory and a slice SEPARATELY. That is a new method, not a format change, which makes M5.66 cheaper than its first framing.' The backlog cell for M5.66 (backlog.md:126) names this very wording as the error it fixed -- 'AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS CELL OVERSTATED IT AS "TWO THINGS IN THE SEGMENT LAYOUT FORBID IT"' -- so the correction reached the row and not the record. (b2) at :222-225 carries the weaker version of the same claim ('no range is expressible') for the same reason.
findings.failure_scenario: 'Alternatives considered' is where a later reader re-prices a rejected option, and M5.66's criterion 3 obliges its owner to revisit Decision (b), which means reading (b1)-(b3). They find the record saying in one place that M5.66 is a new method and not a format change, and in another that the layout FORBIDS two things one of which is the codec id -- the classic signal that a format change is needed. The expensive reading is the one that lives under the option's own heading, so the row gets scoped as a wire change (six golden files, both readers, both writers, three ADRs under non-negotiable 8) or abandoned in favour of removing the fields, which is the arm this record spent four rounds deciding against.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite (b3) to the reason that survives: it is out of scope and wrong-ordered, and what it needs is one new SegmentReader entry point taking a directory and a slice separately -- not a format change. Drop the codec sentence or mark it as ruling out the one-request slice-only form only, as :92-94 and the M5.66 cell already do. Same edit for (b2)'s 'no range is expressible'.

findings.title: The new doc 10 section 8 REVISION BANNER asserts 'a consumer-side ranged read is not currently expressible at all' plus the codec objection -- contradicting the section 7 banner 36 lines above that this commit also wrote
findings.summary: The banner added at :214-223 ends: 'A consumer-side **ranged** read is not currently expressible at all: SegmentReader.open checks the footer magic before the directory, so a prefix throws; and u32 codecFlags lives per run in the directory while DATA carries no codec id, so a ranged GET of a run's DATA slice cannot decompress what it fetched. That is M5.66.' The banner this same commit adds at :183-189 says 'A consumer-side bounded read is TWO expressible requests -- the header range [0, PREAMBLE + headerLen), which is what SegmentKey's h<headerLen> is for, then the run's slice -- and what is missing is only a SegmentReader entry point taking a directory and a slice separately', and the identical sentence was propagated to doc 04 section 2's bullet, doc 13 and 50-open-questions Q8. Section 8 is the one banner it was not propagated to, and it is the section ADR-0044's own Research header line (:6-8) routes a reader to. doc 04's section 2c banner at :242 carries a weaker instance of the same claim ('no ranged GET is expressible').
findings.failure_scenario: AGENTS.md: 'when an early conclusion and a revision banner disagree, the banner wins', and round 1 of this very task blocked on a banner still asserting a retired claim on the ground that M5.66's owner, routed there by the research skill, would implement it. That is the state this banner recreates with the claim inverted: the corpus reader now learns from the newest, highest-authority text on the page that a ranged read is impossible at all and that the segment layout blocks it in two places. M5.66's owner reaches doc 10 sections 7-8 through this ADR's own Research header, meets the section 7 banner and the section 8 banner saying opposite things thirty lines apart, and has nothing to break the tie except which one they read last. The likely outcome is the expensive one -- the row is priced as a format change, or its removal arm is taken -- which is the specific mistake the round-4 correction exists to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the last three lines of the section 8 banner with the sentence already used in the other four banners: a consumer-side bounded read is two expressible requests (header range, then slice), the codec flags come with the directory the header fetch returns, and what is missing is one SegmentReader entry point -- M5.66. Then fix doc 04 section 2c's point (3) the same way: what is dead is coalescing WITHOUT a directory read, not the expressibility of the range.

findings.title: The sweep table M5.66's criterion 3 makes THE enumeration is split in two by a paragraph: seven of nineteen rows fall outside it and do not render as a table
findings.summary: The table opens at :275-276 and runs to :288 (twelve rows). :289 is blank, :290-295 is the paragraph '⚠️ THIS TABLE IS THE SINGLE ENUMERATION, AND ROWS THAT NEED TO ACT ON IT MUST POINT AT IT RATHER THAN COPY IT', :296 is blank, and :297-303 is seven more sweep rows with no header and no |---|---| separator. In rendered Markdown the blank line terminates the table, so those seven rows are a paragraph of literal pipe characters, not a table. The stranded rows are not the trivial ones: doc 04 section 2c's banner (the round-1 BLOCKING finding), SubscriptionEventGrantTest, SegmentReaderTest plus doc 01 section 3, doc 13 sections 4 and 5 (the round-2 finding about a false 'confirmed'), doc 03:153, ADR-0042, and M5 SPEC.md:301.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.66's criterion 3 was rewritten this round to read 'EVERY SITE IN ADR-0044's SWEEP TABLE IS CORRECTED OR RE-CONFIRMED, AND THE TABLE IS THE ENUMERATION', on the stated ground that copying a list goes stale. Its owner opens this record, sees a table, sees a paragraph closing it with the words 'THIS TABLE IS THE SINGLE ENUMERATION', and works twelve rows. The seven below the paragraph read as prose, sit after the sentence that appears to close the table, and are exactly the rows two earlier rounds had to add. The row then marks itself done having re-confirmed twelve of nineteen sites -- the same 'corrected is indistinguishable from not looked at' failure the artifact exists to prevent, now caused by the artifact's own layout. It also defeats the rung-4 fix: the enumeration is again in two places, in the one record that spent five findings saying not to do that.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the paragraph above the table header at :275, or below :303. One table, one enumeration, and the sentence that calls it the single enumeration is not sitting inside it.

findings.title: M5.45f's done-cell calls the modelled 7 bytes MEASURED, and re-derives the figure in the clause that says it does not
findings.summary: The cell reads 'They are kept because they are the only thing making a bounded read possible later, at a MEASURED 7 bytes per event -- byteStart reaches 8,388,608 so 4 uvarint bytes, byteLen averages 5.2 KiB at 1,600 runs so 2, plus a 1-byte presence flag -- 5.4% of the subscription stream and 0.134% of the segment -- ADR-0044 derives it ONCE and this cell does not re-derive it', and then three sentences later: 'The 7 bytes and the 5.4% are MODELLED at the 8 MiB / ~1,600-run segment ... An earlier draft of this cell called the modelled half measured.' Both statements are in the same cell: the word the correction retires is still in the sentence the correction is about, and the derivation inputs (8,388,608, 5.2 KiB, 1,600 runs, 4+2+1) are restated inline immediately after the clause promising not to restate them. ADR-0044:124-129 is unambiguous that 7 bytes is modelled and that only the 128/123 golden pair is measured.
findings.failure_scenario: backlog.md is the authoritative row and its State cell is what a status reader and the milestone review quote. Non-negotiable 4 is that no number is called measured without having been measured; this cell calls a model measured in its leading clause, and a reader quoting the row -- a VERIFIED.md line, an M5.20 sweep, a later ADR -- carries 'MEASURED 7 bytes per event' forward with the qualifier left behind, which is how the ~100-byte estimate that round 2 caught got its authority in the first place. The self-correction three sentences later does not undo it; it documents that the author knew and left the word standing.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete 'MEASURED' from the leading clause (it can simply read 'at 7 bytes per event, MODELLED') and delete the inline re-derivation, which is what the same sentence promises not to do -- ADR-0044:124-141 holds it.

findings.title: M5.66 prices the fields at 5.5% where ADR-0044 derives 5.4%, and the same cell says 5.4% further down
findings.summary: backlog.md:126 opens 'priced at 5.5% of the subscription stream they travel on (0.13% of the segment they describe)' and later in the same cell says 'the coordinates more clearly worth their 5.4%'. ADR-0044:133-143 derives 7/129 = 5.4% and states 'THE DECISION IS TAKEN ON 5.4%'. :106-109 of that record claims 'this is the ONE place it is derived. Every other site points here rather than restating it; three review rounds were spent on copies of this figure disagreeing with each other.' This row is a copy of the figure disagreeing with it, and with itself, in the row the record creates. Separately, ADR-0043's new Status block (:6) restates the price as '0.13% of the segment' -- the denominator ADR-0044:206-207 explicitly says the decision is NOT taken on.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.66's owner reads their own row first (next-task points them at the backlog, not at the ADR) and carries 5.5% into criterion 1's crossover work and into whatever they write next; the next reader comparing the row against the record finds two numbers for one quantity and reopens the arithmetic for a fourth time, which is the specific cost :106-109 says three rounds already paid. Nothing decides differently at 5.4 versus 5.5, which is why this is minor rather than major.
findings.suggested_fix: Make both mentions in the cell point rather than restate: 'priced in ADR-0044 (5.4% of the subscription stream, derived once there)'. Drop the 0.13% from ADR-0043's Status or replace it with the stream figure the decision is taken on.

findings.title: headerRangeEndInclusive is cited in four places as the proof the consumer can name the header range, and it lives in `ingest`, which the consumer path may not depend on
findings.summary: The claim is true as written -- SegmentPublisher:147 does compute PREAMBLE_BYTES + SegmentKey.headerLenOf(key) - 1 -- but SegmentPublisher is in `ingest`, and client/build.gradle.kts declares exactly api(project(":format")) while plugin/build.gradle.kts declares api(project(":client")) with `ingest` only as testImplementation. So no consumer-side production code can call it. What IS reachable is what actually makes the claim hold: SegmentKey.headerLenOf and SegmentFormat.PREAMBLE_BYTES are both public in `format`, and SubscriptionEvent carries segmentKey. The same sentence now appears in ADR-0044:86, backlog.md:126, doc 10:184 and doc 13:105.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.66's owner takes the cited method as the thing to reuse, discovers `client` may not depend on `ingest` (ADR-0023 and check-module), and either duplicates the computation -- two places computing one wire-format range, which is how the preamble/headerLen relationship drifts -- or spends the row moving a method out of the ingester. Naming the `format` primitives instead makes the reuse obvious and keeps the citation honest about which side of the seam it lives on.
findings.suggested_fix: Add half a clause where the claim is derived (ADR-0044:86): '... and SegmentPublisher.headerRangeEndInclusive computes it in the tree today, ingester-side; the consumer's half is SegmentKey.headerLenOf plus SegmentFormat.PREAMBLE_BYTES, both public in `format`.'

findings.title: The new class javadoc and the new .as() message assert the retired 'no range is expressible' claim, in a file the sweep table lists as Corrected
findings.summary: The javadoc added at :21-27 reads 'the grant is scoped to one key and to NO range, because no range is expressible -- SegmentReader.open checks the footer magic before the directory, so a prefix throws, and nothing the consumer holds carries the object length', and the assertion description rewritten at :279-282 ends 'no ranged GET is expressible'. Both are the claim ADR-0044:80-99 corrects, written by this commit, in the file the sweep table at :298 disposition as 'Corrected'. It is the same defect as r4-1 and r4-3 one layer down; it is minor because a test javadoc misdirects a narrower audience than a corpus banner or the ADR's own decision, and because the assertions themselves are untouched and correct.
findings.failure_scenario: The next reader of this test -- most likely M5.66's owner, since the sweep table sends them here to re-confirm it -- reads that no range is expressible and that the two stated layout facts are why, and carries that into the row, the same way the retired claim travelled from ADR-0043 into four documents and three rounds of this review. The file is also the one the sweep marks as already corrected, so nothing later points at it again.
findings.suggested_fix: Same replacement as r4-1: the grant is scoped to one key and to no range because the only read the consumer path makes is a whole-object GET; a bounded read is two expressible requests and M5.66 owns the reader that would use them.
